channel.title: Denis Pirollo for Mayor of Hawkesbury
channel.description: Denis Pirollo is running for Mayor of Hawkesbury, Ontario. Voting day is Monday, October 26, 2026. Five points: fix the worst roads first; revitalize Main Street, waterfront, festivals; keep our young people and jobs; build somewhere to live; open the books.

item.title: Six years of council records, and not one vote shows who voted which way
item.description: Six years of council records, and not one vote shows who voted which way. It is entirely lawful, and it can end the day somebody asks. The plan to put every vote on the big things on the record, with names, where you can look it up.

item.title: We share a bridge. Let's share a table.
item.description: What Hawkesbury already signs with the Counties, Champlain and the Quebec side, where nobody sits at a table yet, and the five moves a mayor can make with council toward Ottawa and Montreal.

item.title: Half full on a dry day: what our pipes and our power can really take
item.description: The sewage plant ran at about half of its rating last year, the water plant used less than a third on its busiest day, and Hydro One sees room for homes until 2037. The real limits are storms, one big factory and the lights. And the one number nobody has printed.

item.title: Nearly two parking spaces for a bachelor apartment: the rules that stop homes here
item.description: For twenty years our population went down while the towns around us grew. The land being cleaned right now, the town rules a council can change on its own, and the people Denis will get on the phone himself.

item.title: The college already trains here. The hospital already hires. The campus that connects them.
item.description: Points 2, 3 and 4 taken all the way. What a bilingual trades and health-care campus could be, built on the training that already happens here. And an honest account of what a mayor could and could not do about it.

item.title: Worst streets first, every outside dollar chased: the roads plan
item.description: What the Town's own plan says, who is responsible for each piece of the fix, and the seven moves a mayor can actually make with council.

item.title: 130 acres next door wait on our pipes. A builder's plan to finish them.
item.description: Next door in Champlain, 130 acres of zoned industrial land waits on one thing: our water and sewer. The two towns signed a first agreement in December, the deadline for the final one slipped, and finishing is a builder's trade.

item.title: The typical resident is thirteen years older than twenty years ago. The plan to turn that around.
item.description: The typical person in town today is thirteen years older than the typical person here twenty years ago. A first job at town hall, a real seat at the table, and the young talent already carrying this campaign.

item.title: Zero buses. One law. Four votes.
item.description: The intercity bus left and never came back, the Counties' bus shut down, and a lot of people here do not drive. The one by-law a mayor can fix from inside Town Hall, the study money that exists, and five moves in the order I will try them.

item.title: Town Hall costs 37 percent more than five years ago. The audit that finds out why.
item.description: Running Town Hall costs 37 percent more than five years ago. No line in the books says what technology costs. The audit that counts the hours, the services going online, and the promise that nobody loses a job over it.

item.title: The mayor has one vote of seven. Here is what the job can actually do.
item.description: One vote of seven. The pen that writes the budget. A seat on the county council. And powers sitting in a drawer. The parts of the job nobody campaigns on, plus a test to hold every candidate to.

item.title: The tourism line in the budget reads $0. Here is who fixes that.
item.description: The tourism line in the Town's budget reads $0. The plan puts the street, the river and the events calendar under one person in charge, one set of rules, and one clear list of what a sponsor gets.

item.title: Months inside the Town's budgets: what checks out, and what nobody can check
item.description: We spent months inside the Town's budgets and its own rules. Here is what checks out, what cannot be checked, and the commitments that would let anyone here check the Town's numbers for themselves.
